The test image shows a corn husk/ear with small dark brown to black oval/round spots scattered on green tissue, with some tan discoloration. The spots appear embedded in the tissue. Top candidates: **Tar_spot** (black raised stromata on husks), **Physoderma_brown_spot** (dark oval spots), or **Anthracnose_leaf_spot_top_dieback**.

Let me view reference images for the top candidates in parallel.

The tar spot reference shows very tiny densely packed black dots; the physoderma shows dark spots on green tissue; anthracnose shows elongated tan lesions. The test image shows discrete dark oval/round spots on husk tissue. Let me check a couple more candidates.

Key observations from the test image:
- Central structure appears to be a young corn ear wrapped in husk, or possibly a leaf sheath
- Dark brown to black, discrete oval/round spots scattered on the green surface
- Some tan/yellow discoloration at margins
- Spots appear moderate sized (~3-5mm), not the tiny pepper-speck size of tar spot

**Comparing candidates:**
- **Tar_spot**: Reference shows extremely tiny, very numerous black dots (pepper-grain sized) — the test image spots are larger and fewer
- **Physoderma_brown_spot**: Reference top-left panel shows dark brown-black oval spots on green stalk/sheath tissue — very similar to the test image's spot appearance and size
- **Anthracnose_leaf_spot**: Shows more elongated spindle lesions with prominent tan centers — doesn't match
- **Eyespot/Holcus_spot**: Yellow halos, tan centers — doesn't match the dark color

The dark oval spots on green husk/sheath tissue most closely matches Physoderma_brown_spot, specifically the darker lesions that appear on midrib and sheath tissues. The spots in the test image have the characteristic dark purplish-black oval appearance described for Physoderma on non-blade tissue.
